clear.does: clear rough ground for a field: the work keeps between days and adds up across workers; when it is done the ground is a field, fallow and unbroken, and yours if nobody held it
clear.aware: turning meadow, pasture or scrub into a new field
clear.rough: Done on meadow, pasture or scrub with a tool in hand; bare hands go slowly. It takes many days before the ground is a field.
clear.capable: A better tool and practice clear more a day, and the tool wears. Others' work on the same ground adds to yours. Scrub takes far longer than grass.
clear.known: Cleared meadow starts richer than cleared scrub. Hoe or plough the new field before sowing. Clearing ground someone already holds makes it their field, not yours.

clear for building.does: clear open ground or scrub for building: the work keeps and adds up across workers; when it is done it is built ground, farmland no longer, and yours if nobody held it
clear for building.aware: making ground ready to build houses on
clear for building.rough: Done with a tool in hand on field, pasture, meadow or scrub; refused while a crop stands there. Bare hands go slowly.
clear for building.capable: A better tool and practice clear more a day, and the tool wears. Others' work adds to yours. Scrub, with its roots, takes far longer than grass.
clear for building.known: Built ground takes houses but never a crop or grazing again: its grass, crop and holdings end with the clearing. Clear only what you mean to build on.

clear the leat.does: clear the mill leat of silt and weed: a choked leat leaves the water mill grinding less from the same work until it is cleared
clear the leat.aware: keeping a water mill's channel clear so it runs
clear the leat.rough: Done at a water wheel; it needs no materials. The leat silts with time, not with use, so even an idle mill needs it.
clear the leat.capable: Clearing it before it is choked is not wasted: it starts the reckoning afresh. Either a choked leat or worn millstones slows the grinding, so see to both.
clear the leat.known: The leat silts by the year and the stones wear by the grain put through, so they fall due at different times: keep a reckoning of each.

dig a strip.does: break the turf of a strip of meadow or pasture you hold, so flax sown there takes as on a field; the meadow stays a meadow
dig a strip.aware: breaking turf for a small flax patch
dig a strip.rough: Only on meadow or pasture you or yours hold. Sow flax seed on it after; seed thrown on unbroken turf mostly comes to nothing.
dig a strip.capable: Practice breaks more a day, up to the largest strip a holding may have; past that it is refused. Sow no more than a strip's worth of flax seed there.
dig a strip.known: The dug turf waits for the seed and is used up by the sowing. Flax sown thicker than a strip becomes the main crop, and takes the turf's loss.

ditch.does: ditch and bank wet ground: crew work, anyone may dig, led by one who knows how
ditch.aware: draining wet ground so a field bears fully
ditch.rough: Only on wet ground. A day's digging holds only if someone who knows how works on the ditches that same day; otherwise it is lost.
ditch.capable: A tool and practice dig more, and the tool wears. The more of the field ditched, the nearer it bears to good ground. Finished ditches want mending each season.
ditch.known: Unmended through a season, finished ditches fall in by a share and must be dug again. Once whole and kept for the season, more work is refused.

dress millstones.does: recut the furrows of worn millstones: worn stones grind less from the same work until they are dressed
dress millstones.aware: recutting millstones so they grind well again
dress millstones.rough: Done at the millstones; it needs no materials. They wear by the grain put through them, so a busy mill needs it sooner.
dress millstones.capable: Dressing stones not yet worn is not wasted: it starts their wear afresh. At a water mill a choked leat slows the grinding too, whatever the stones.
dress millstones.known: Worn stones take the full work for a lesser grist, so every day ground on them is part lost: dress them before a heavy grinding, not after.

fence.does: put a fence round a parcel, timber going in with the work; when it is finished, with its gate shut, it keeps beasts in and out
fence.aware: a fence round a field holding beasts in or out
fence.rough: Needs timber to hand as you work; a tool helps. It holds nothing until finished, and where a wall stands it is refused.
fence.capable: Anyone's work counts and adds up over days. Once standing, work on it is mending: unmended through a year it grows gappy, then falls, and gappy lets beasts through.
fence.known: A fallen fence is rebuilt from what still stands, so mend it before it goes. It keeps out large raiders by night, but small beasts slip through any fence.
grounded_in: cybertron2/engine/farm.py _fence: timber consumed in proportion to the work; built fence: mend

guard the field.does: sit up by a field all night to scare beasts off, with a fire, clappers, a horn or the dog; you lose the night's sleep
guard the field.aware: sitting up all night to keep beasts off crops
guard the field.rough: Needs something to scare with: wood for a fire, clappers or a horn to hand, or a dog at home. You will be tired tomorrow.
guard the field.capable: Name the scare, else the first you have is used, and a fire burns its wood. A watch lasts one night; hungry or bold beasts turn less.
guard the field.known: Some beasts grow used to a scare used night after night, so change it. Watching the gap they come in by turns them sooner. Herded beasts count as watched.

herd.does: watch a herd on its grazing for the day: herded beasts do not wander, and a herder holds far more head together than beasts left alone
herd.aware: watching the beasts so they keep together
herd.rough: Done where the beasts are. Unnamed, it is yours or your household's; name another's herd to watch it. Once watched enough today, it is refused.
herd.capable: Left alone a big herd breaks into groups that stray into crops and onto the roads; each herder holds a good number together, so a large herd wants more.
herd.known: A herd watched by day also counts as watched when raiders come for it that night. A ripe crop near pulls even fed beasts far: herd them then.

hoe.does: break a field's soil with a hoe, turning up stones: broken ground sown bears more; over a standing crop it turns the crop under
hoe.aware: breaking up field soil by hand for sowing
hoe.rough: Done on a field, best with a tool in hand. Hoeing where a crop stands turns it under, ripe or green, and it is gone.
hoe.capable: A better tool and practice break more, and the tool wears. Break unsown ground and sow it: broken soil bears more. The stones turned up are yours.
hoe.known: Turning under a failed or unwanted crop frees the ground for seed and feeds the soil a little, the more the further it grew. A plough breaks far more.
grounded_in: cybertron2/engine/farm.py _break: broken plots, stone created (D2-56); refused when all broken

manure.does: spread dung on a field's plots: the soil comes back toward its best, the more the poorer it is, never past what that ground can be
manure.aware: spreading dung to feed tired soil
manure.rough: Done on a field, with dung to hand; gather it where beasts stand. Soil already good gains little from it.
manure.capable: Practice covers more ground each go. On a large holding each go lifts the whole soil less, so spread often. Beasts in stalls keep more dung for you.
manure.known: Poor land stays poor: dung lifts a soil only toward what that ground can be. Beans after grain, or a rest, restore it too; dung serves ground you cannot rest.

mend the brine pan.does: patch and reset a burnt-through brine pan: a worn pan boils less salt from the same work until it is mended
mend the brine pan.aware: patching the salt pan when it burns through
mend the brine pan.rough: Done at the brine pan, with a little copper in your own hands; copper in a store is not reached. It wears with each boiling.
mend the brine pan.capable: Mending a pan not yet burnt through is not wasted: it starts its wear afresh. Count your boilings and mend it before it fails.
mend the brine pan.known: Keep copper by you for it: a worn pan takes the full work for less salt, so every boiling on it is part lost.

milk.does: milk the cows in milk of a herd: the milk is yours, and those one milker leaves, another may milk the same day
milk.aware: drawing milk from cows that have calved
milk.rough: Only where a cow in milk is; unnamed, only your own or your household's herd. Milk does not keep long.
milk.capable: Practice draws more from each cow. A cow comes into milk when she calves, which needs a bull with fed cows; she dries off with time, faster when hungry.
milk.known: Milk spoils fast: drink it, or make cheese with salt. Kill a cow in milk and her milk goes with her; a hungry winter dries the herd.

open the gate.does: open a gate in a fence and leave it standing open: beasts pass freely in and out until it is shut, and it is noticed
open the gate.rough: Only where a fence stands whole enough to have a gate, and the gate is shut. It takes no work.
open the gate.capable: An open gate lets a herd wander through as if no fence stood, in or out, until someone shuts it.
open the gate.known: Who left it open is marked with the gate, and the land's holders are concerned in it: open another's gate only with cause.

pest work.does: go over a crop and take off what is eating it; name the pest with "looking for", else the worst there
pest work.aware: picking pests off a growing crop
pest work.rough: Done on a growing crop, or on meadow grass for moles. Name the pest, else the worst there is taken.
pest work.capable: Slugs come out at dusk: a tallow light in hand lets you work on into the dark and take more, and burns down. The good lasts only some days.
pest work.known: The grey spiny grubs on beans are ladybird young that eat the fly: name them and you kill your helpers. Beasts are no pests: watch the field for those.
grounded_in: cybertron2/engine/wild.py pest: named by 'looking for' (methods.LOAD_NAMES), else the worst load that harms this ground's crop or grass, never the ladybirds unasked; raiders refused toward guard the field

And the name 'grubs' (LOAD_NAMES) means the ladybirds, so 'looking for: grubs' thins the ladybirds, a help to the fly. The row's needs.on_crop is read nowhere.

plough.aware: breaking a field with oxen and a plough
plough.rough: Needs a yoked pair of oxen you may use here, a wooden plough and harness to hand. Ploughing a sown field turns its crop under.
plough.capable: Practice breaks more a day. The plough wears by the ground broken, the harness by each day's work; others' oxen may be used, but it is seen.
plough.known: Plough unsown ground before sowing: broken soil bears more. A spare harness and plough keep the team working when one wears out; harness is made from timber and hide.

pull flax.known: Ret the straw before it is spun. Keep back the rippled seed for next year's strip; sown thicker than a strip, flax becomes a field's main crop.

reap.does: reap a standing crop: ripe, it gives its grain or beans, with straw for fodder from grain and rye; cut green, it gives green fodder
reap.aware: cutting a ripe crop to bring in the harvest
reap.rough: Done where a crop stands, best with a tool in hand. Cut before it is ripe and you get green fodder, little food.
reap.capable: A better tool and practice cut more a day, and the tool wears. Weeding beforehand raises what it gives. Left past its time it rots night by night.
reap.known: A crop is nobody's until reaped: whoever reaps another's plots takes the grain, and is seen. A blighted crop gives nothing. Keep grain from vermin.

repair.does: mend a building's damage: its stuff goes in when the mending starts, then the work, until it is a step sounder; a sound building is refused
repair.aware: mending a damaged house or building
repair.rough: Needs its stuff, timber or stone as it is built, to hand or in its store. Mending stone is walling, which you must know.
repair.capable: The work keeps between days until done; practice does more each time. A worn house lets in damp, a holed one lets foxes and rats in, shut or not.
repair.known: Storms, frost and neglect wear buildings, and unmended damage worsens: mend early. A weir is mended a section at a time.

select seed.does: go through a ripe crop marking the best ears for seed: once you know it fully, the crops you sow ripen sooner
select seed.aware: choosing the best ears for next year's seed
select seed.rough: Needs a ripe crop in a field; once you have been through a crop, going through it again is refused.
select seed.capable: It is the knowing that pays, not the marking: practise on every ripe crop you can until you know it fully.
select seed.known: A sooner crop can beat the frost or let another sowing into the year. The marked ears change nothing; it is your own sowings that gain.

shut.does: shut up your house, store and hens for the night
shut.aware: shutting up house, store and hens against night raiders
shut.rough: Done on built ground, for tonight only; it shuts every house of yours that has a store. Do it each evening.
shut.capable: A shut door keeps out most of what comes for hens or grain; left open, much gets in. A dog at home turns raiders too.
shut.known: Shutting is no help to a holed house: beasts small enough come through its gaps anyway, so mend the walls. A cat in the store keeps vermin down.

shut the gate.does: shut a gate in a fence: the fence holds beasts in, and keeps them out, as well as it stands
shut the gate.aware: closing a field gate to keep beasts in
shut the gate.rough: Only where a fence stands and its gate is open. It takes no work.
shut the gate.capable: A shut gate holds as well as its fence: a gappy fence still lets some through, shut or not.
shut the gate.known: Beasts that strayed come home at dusk only at the fence's odds while the gate round home is shut; a hungry herd stays out after food.

slaughter.does: kill a beast of a herd: its meat, hide and tallow come to you, in your hands or the store you work for, and the herd is one fewer
slaughter.aware: killing a beast for meat, hide and tallow
slaughter.rough: Say which beast, cow, ox, bull or calf, or which herd; unnamed it is refused. Name another's herd and you kill theirs, seen.
slaughter.capable: Named by herd alone, a calf goes first. Fresh meat spoils fast: salt, smoke or dry it soon, or eat it. A cow in milk takes her milk with her.
slaughter.known: Hide makes harness, packs and bedding; tallow makes lights for night work. Keep the cows and a bull: without them the herd bears no calves.

sow.does: sow seed broadcast on your plots of a field, then the unclaimed plots: it grows into a crop to weed and reap
sow.aware: throwing seed on ground to grow a crop
sow.rough: Say which seed. Ground with another crop standing must be reaped or turned under first. Seed thrown on unbroken turf mostly comes to nothing.
sow.capable: Sow on hoed or ploughed ground for more; tired soil gives less. The same crop twice running fails more often. Seed in cold ground lies, a little lost each night.
sow.known: A master sower's crops bear more. Beans after grain rest the soil. A small sowing of flax seed goes into a strip beside the main crop.

tend the smoke.does: feed and bank a smokehouse fire for the night: only a tended night counts toward what hangs there; untended, the fire dies and what hangs spoils
tend the smoke.aware: keeping a smokehouse fire going overnight
tend the smoke.rough: Only where something hangs smoking, once a day. Firewood must be there: with too little for the night the fire dies anyway.
tend the smoke.capable: Firewood in your hands goes on if the store is short. Tend it every day until the lot is done, then take it down.
tend the smoke.known: Each night it burns, the fire may catch the smokehouse and what hangs in it, a wattle one most: build it of timber or stone, apart from the houses.

terrace.does: terrace hill ground: crew work, anyone may dig, led by one who knows how
terrace.aware: building terraces so hill ground bears fully
terrace.rough: Only on hill ground, with stone to hand. A day's work holds only if someone who knows how works on it that day.
terrace.capable: A tool and practice do more, and the tool wears. The more terraced, the nearer the field bears to good ground. Finished terraces want mending each season, and stone.
terrace.known: Unmended through a season, finished terraces fall in by a share. Stones a hoe or plough turns up serve. Once whole and kept for the season, more work is refused.

wall.does: wall a parcel round in dry stone: crew work, anyone may work on it, led by one who knows how
wall.aware: a dry-stone wall round a field, holding beasts best
wall.rough: Needs stone to hand, going in with the work. A day's work holds only if someone who knows walling works on it that day.
wall.capable: A tool and practice lay more, and the tool wears. A finished wall holds beasts far better than a fence, keeps most raiders out, and does not rot.
wall.known: Walling is the mason's craft too: building or mending in stone needs it. Where a fence stands the wall is refused. A finished wall wants no yearly mending.

weed.does: weed a growing crop: a cleaner crop bears more when reaped, up to as clean as weeding makes it
weed.aware: pulling weeds so a crop bears more
weed.rough: Done on a growing crop; it needs no tool. Weeding a ripe crop does it no good, and the day is wasted.
weed.capable: Practice weeds more ground each go. Each weeding gains less than the last, and a large crop takes many goes to come clean.
weed.known: Past clean it gains nothing: stop and spend the day elsewhere. A crop withered by blight is refused; a strip beside the main crop is never weeded.
